We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999 (we can't check price but assume typical). Need to construct route using templates.

We have some building blocks: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1) is buyable (true). Also aniline (c1ccc(N)cc1) is buyable. Also C=CC(=O)Cl (acryloyl chloride) is buyable. Also maybe 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually we have sulfonyl chloride with tolyl group, we need to attach sulfonamide to another aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The target has sulfonamide linking two aryl groups: tolyl-sulfonyl attached to an aniline of second ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) where the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to that second ring (i.e., NS(=O)(=O)Ar). So we can make sulfonamide by reacting tolyl sulfonyl chloride with an aniline (p-aminophenyl) that also bears the side chain (C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N). So we need to prepare that aniline with side chain.

The side chain is a cinnamoyl amide attached to an aniline (para position). So we need an aniline (c2ccc(N)cc2) with a para amide of a trans-α,β-unsaturated carbonyl (C=CC(=O)N-phenyl). Actually the side chain is attached to the aromatic ring via the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the aniline (c2ccc(... )cc2) has at para position a vinyl amide: -CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (an aniline attached to carbonyl). So we need to synthesize that aniline with side chain.

We could start from 4-aminobenzaldehyde? But we need vinyl amide. Could do Heck coupling of an aryl bromide with acrylamide? Actually we can make the side chain via condensation of 4-aminobenzaldehyde with a suitable amide? Another approach: start from 4-aminobenzyl bromide and do Wittig? Might be complex.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-aminobenzaldehyde (C6H4(N)CHO). Then perform Knoevenagel condensation with malonic acid derivative? Not.

Maybe easier: Use commercially available 4-aminocinnamic acid (p-aminocinnamic acid) which is C=CC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1? Actually p-aminocinnamic acid is NH2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH. Not same.

But we need amide with anilide: C=CC(=O)N-Ph-NH2. That's N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide? Wait: C=CC(=O)N-Ph-NH2 where Ph is phenyl with NH2 at para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline attached to carbonyl nitrogen (i.e., anilide with an extra NH2 on phenyl). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring that also has an NH2 substituent (para?). The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with two amino groups? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (as substituent) and also there is an NH at the other end? Wait: "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the aromatic ring has an NH attached at position 1 (the first N) and also an NH2 at position? Actually the SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino group attached to the aromatic carbon (the first N) and also an amino group attached to the aromatic carbon at the other end? The pattern is N-Ph-N (two nitrogens attached to the same phenyl ring at positions 1 and maybe 4). So it's p-phenylenediamine? Actually p-phenylenediamine SMILES is "Nc1ccc(N)cc1". Yes that's same as "Nc3ccccc3N". So the amide nitrogen is attached to p-phenylenediamine (para-diaminobenzene). So the amide is N-(p-phenylenediamine)acrylamide.

Thus the side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2) (para-diamine). So we need p-phenylenediamine (commercial) and acryloyl chloride to make the amide (acrylamide). Then we need to do a Heck coupling to attach the vinyl group to the aromatic ring (the same p-phenylenediamine? Actually the vinyl is attached to the aromatic ring via the double bond: /C=C/ attached to the aromatic ring at the carbon bearing the sulfonamide? Wait the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the aromatic ring (c2ccc...cc2) has a substituent at para position: /C=C/C(=O)N-p-phenylenediamine. So the vinyl carbon attached directly to the aromatic ring (aryl-alkene). So we need to form a styryl amide via Heck coupling of p-phenylenediamine amide (acrylamide) with aryl bromide (4-bromo-? Actually we need aryl bromide of the second ring). So we could start from 4-bromo-p-phenylenediamine? Wait the second ring is the one bearing the side chain; it also has the sulfonamide attached at para position? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to that ring via nitrogen (NSO2). The second ring is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonamide nitrogen. So the second ring is an aniline (attached to sulfonyl). It also has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonamide? In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to the aromatic carbon (c2). The side chain is para to that? Not important.

Thus we need to construct the second ring with both sulfonamide nitrogen attached and the vinyl amide substituent. Could be built by first forming the vinyl amide on a phenyl ring (p-aminophenyl) then sulfonylate the aniline nitrogen.

Simplify route: Step 1: Prepare N-(p-phenylenediamine)acrylamide: React acryloyl chloride (C=CC(=O)Cl) with p-phenylenediamine (Nc1ccc(N)cc1) to give a monoacrylamide (one amine acylated). This yields C=CC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (the amide). This is commercially maybe not but we can make.

Step 2: Perform Heck coupling of this acrylamide (as alkene) with 4-bromo-? Actually we need to attach the alkene to the aromatic ring that will later be sulfonylated. The acrylamide already has the alkene attached to carbonyl, not to aromatic. Wait the acrylamide is CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). The double bond is at the terminal (CH2=CH-). In target, the double bond is attached to aromatic ring: Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). So we need to connect the alkene to aromatic ring via a C-C bond at the terminal carbon of the alkene (the CH2). This is a Heck coupling of aryl bromide with the alkene (acrylamide) to give trans-aryl-alkene. So we need aryl bromide: 4-bromo-? The aryl that will later be sulfonylated is tolyl (with methyl). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to tolyl sulfonyl chloride, not the second ring. Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl sulfonyl group, not the second ring. The second ring is attached to sulfonamide nitrogen, not to sulfonyl chloride. So the second ring is the aniline that is sulfonylated. So we need to sulfonylate that aniline after we have the vinyl amide attached.

Thus we need aniline (p-aminophenyl) with vinyl amide at para position (or meta). Starting from 4-bromo-2-methylaniline? Actually the second ring does not have methyl; the methyl is on the first ring (tolyl). So the second ring is just phenyl with amine (attached to sulfonyl) and the vinyl amide substituent. So we can start from 4-bromoaniline (Brc1ccc(N)cc1). This is buyable (we saw true). Then perform Heck coupling with acryloyl chloride? Actually need acrylamide as alkene partner: we can use N-(p-phenylenediamine)acrylamide as alkene, but that already contains an aniline (NH2) which may interfere. Better: Use acryloyl chloride to make acryloyl amide with p-phenylenediamine? Wait we need the amide attached to phenyl with NH2 (the second phenyl). The amide nitrogen is attached to p-phenylenediamine, not to the aryl that will be sulfonylated. So the acrylamide's aromatic part is p-phenylenediamine (which has an extra NH2). That's fine.

Thus route:

Leaf 1: p-phenylenediamine (Nc1ccc(N)cc1) – buyable.

Leaf 2: acryloyl chloride (C=CC(=O)Cl) – buyable.

Leaf 3: 4-bromo-2-methylbenzene? Actually we need toluene sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) as sulfonylating agent: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 – buyable (we saw true).

Leaf 4: 4-bromoaniline (Brc1ccc(N)cc1) – buyable (true). This will be the aromatic ring that gets sulfonylated and also undergo Heck coupling.

But we need both sulfonylation and Heck coupling on same aniline. Could do sulfonylation first (react aniline with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) to give sulfonamide (target first part). Then perform Heck coupling on the aromatic ring (which still has bromine) to attach the vinyl amide. However sulfonamide may affect Heck but likely okay.

Thus steps:

Step A (reaction 1): Sulfonylation: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + 4-bromoaniline → Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? Wait product would be Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? Actually sulfonyl chloride reacts with aniline to give sulfonamide: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? No, the sulfonyl chloride attaches to N, losing Cl, giving Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1? The product is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1? But we need NS(=O)(=O) attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group, not chlorine. So product is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1. Reaction with aniline gives Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1 (the sulfonamide). The product still has bromine on the aniline? Wait the aniline is 4-bromoaniline, so after sulfonylation we have Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) )cc1 with bromine at para? The SMILES would be Cc1ccc(N(S(=O)(=O)C) )c(Br) c1? Actually need to combine: tolyl sulfonyl group attached to aniline which also has bromine at para relative to N? The aniline is Brc1ccc(N)cc1. After sulfonylation, the N becomes N-SO2-tolyl, and the bromine remains at the para position (relative to N). So product SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)C)cc1? Wait the tolyl group is attached to sulfonyl, not the aromatic ring. So product: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)N(c2ccc(Br)cc2))cc1? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the tolyl ring, not the aniline. So the product is tolyl-sulfonyl attached to aniline: Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)N c2ccc(Br)cc2)cc1. That's the sulfonamide intermediate.

Step B (reaction 2): Heck coupling between the bromine on the aniline ring and the acryloyl amide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2)). Need to generate the acryloyl amide (acrylamide) from acryloyl chloride + p-phenylenediamine (monoacylated). Reaction: acryloyl chloride + p-phenylen diamine → C=CC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (monoamide). This is a separate step (could be done before coupling). So we have leaf 1 and leaf 2 produce intermediate amide.

Step C (reaction 3): Heck coupling of intermediate sulfonamide (aryl bromide) with the acrylamide to give final product.

Thus total 3 steps, leaves are commercially available: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride, 4-bromoaniline, acryloyl chloride, p-phenylenediamine. All buyable.

We need to verify templates for sulfonylation (sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide) and amide formation (acyl chloride + amine) and Heck coupling (aryl bromide + alkene). We need template IDs. We can search for templates matching these transformations.
